question: Has the federal government really stopped sending paper checks?
answer: Mostly, not entirely. Executive Order 14247 (signed March 25, 2025 · published March 28, 2025) ordered an end to paper checks for federal payments, and a customs notice of July 8, 2026 says the government no longer sends them; but the Treasury's own April 29, 2026 proposal still sets out when agencies may send one, and the PBGC was moving its remaining paper-check recipients on June 24, 2026. In FY2026 Treasury screened >1.1 billion payment requests (about $3.7 trillion) before the money went out.

sections.title: How the paper check was phased out
sections.sub: Federal Register and agency records in the library, oldest first. An executive order shows its signing date first.

rows.what: Executive Order 14247 — Modernizing Payments To and From America's Bank Account
rows.detail: Directs the Treasury to cease issuing paper checks for all Federal disbursements and to move every payment into and out of the U.S. General Fund — “America's bank account” — onto electronic rails, to the extent permitted by law. Frames paper checks as a source of cost, delay, fraud, and theft. The founding order of the payment-rails rewiring.

rows.what: Request for Information on Implementing EO 14247 (Modernizing Payments)
rows.detail: Treasury invites public input on implementing the President's order to end paper checks, with emphasis on a public-awareness campaign to move unbanked and underbanked recipients onto digital payments. Effective date for ceasing paper disbursements set at September 30, 2025.

rows.what: Transition to Electronic Payments and Disbursements (DOL)
rows.detail: The Department of Labor announces that effective September 30, 2025 it will no longer accept or issue paper checks, citing EO 14247. One of dozens of agency notices that rolled out across government through 2025 — the order propagating into every corner of federal payments (HHS/FDA, DOT/PHMSA, and others followed).

rows.what: Treasury Turns On FedNow for Federal Disbursements (Digital Payout)
rows.detail: The Fiscal Service enables FedNow for federal agency payouts — eight-plus agencies live, FEMA pushing disaster money instantly instead of mailing checks. The state itself now pays citizens over the Fed's instant rail: Treasury and Fed plumbing fused at the retail edge, the completion of the EO 14247 arc.

rows.what: Designation of the Social Security Administration's Numerical Identification System (Numident) Into Do Not Pay
rows.detail: Pursuant to the Payment Integrity Information Act of 2019 (PIIA) (31 U.S.C. 3351 et seq.), the U.S. Department of Treasury (Treasury) operates the Do Not Pay Working System--a centralized portal through which agencies can search multiple databases to verify payment or award eligibility. Treasury, under a delegation from the Director of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB), is authorized to designate new databases for inclusion in the Do Not Pay Working System. Treasury is issuing this Notice of Proposed Designation to provide the public an opportunity to comment on the proposed designation of the Social Security Administration's Numerical Identification System (Numident) to the Do Not Pay Working System.

rows.who: Treasury Department — Bureau of the Fiscal Service
rows.detail: The Bureau of the Fiscal Service proposes amending the regulation that sets the limited circumstances under which paper-check disbursements may still be made by federal agencies — narrowing the exceptions and recasting the Direct Express card and U.S. Debit Card as mere examples of a broader “Treasury-sponsored account.” This is the actual machinery of how Treasury pays the country.

rows.what: Privacy Act System of Records — Do Not Pay (EO 14249)
rows.detail: Implements Executive Order 14249, “Protecting America's Bank Account Against Fraud, Waste, and Abuse,” and OMB Memorandum M-25-32 by adding a routine use to personnel records for the Treasury “Do Not Pay” system — the screening layer bolted onto the new all-electronic disbursement pipe.

rows.what: PBGC: Direct Express Enrollment for Remaining Paper-Check Recipients
rows.detail: The pension agency files the form that moves its last paper-check benefit recipients onto electronic payment, 'to comply with Executive Order 14247.' The Check's implementation now shows up in other agencies' paperwork — the Fiscal Service itself has gone silent in the Register.

rows.what: Federal Reserve Payments Study: 2025 Initial Findings
rows.detail: The Fed's triennial payments study drops its first numbers — the official body count on the death of the paper check and the migration of the country onto electronic rails.

rows.what: CBP: 'The Federal Government No Longer Disburses Paper Checks'
rows.detail: A customs notice states it flatly, in passing: the federal government no longer disburses paper checks; refunds go out electronically via ACH, per the January 2026 Electronic Refunds rule (91 FR 21). The check's obituary, written in a footnote on the far side of the government.

rows.what: The Government Learns Who Is Dead — Payment Verification Goes Government-Wide
rows.detail: Treasury and the Bureau of the Fiscal Service announce that a government-wide payment verification process to stop federal payments to deceased individuals is now implemented. No Federal Register document, no rule — an announcement that a screen has been switched on across the whole disbursement machine. It sits directly downstream of EO 14247 and the Do Not Pay system of records, and it is the same grammar as the check kill: the payment stops being a thing the government sends and becomes a thing the government first checks.

uncertain: Two readings in the record: the customs notice (July 8, 2026) says paper checks have stopped, while the Treasury's proposed rule (April 29, 2026) keeps limited exceptions and the PBGC notice (June 24, 2026) refers to remaining paper-check recipients. The library's order-status reading for EO 14247 is: most disbursements electronic · exceptions remain.
The library has no record of the Treasury disbursement proposal (April 29, 2026) becoming a final rule.
The Federal Reserve Payments Study row carries no numbers in the master; the check-volume figures it reports are not shown here.

Screening numbers: A match is not an eligibility decision. A returned request is not an ACH return, final denial, fraud finding, recovered dollar or audited saving. Future-ledger seams describe what a permissioned provenance layer could record; they are not deployed-system claims.

research.title: Do Not Pay flags payments, but each program makes the call
research.answer: Treasury's Payment Verification system is now an operating government-wide gate: it screens requests before disbursement and can return them to the originating agency.

research.title: No public record yet follows a federal dollar all the way down
research.answer: Federal money does not run through one state pipe. Congress, OMB, federal agencies, recipients, pass-through bodies, payment operators and auditors own different decisions and records.
